name: Lateral parapatellar approach to the distal femur
corridor: Longitudinal lateral parapatellar retinacular and quadriceps split with medial patellar dislocation

positioning.text: Position supine on a radiolucent table with a towel roll supporting approximately 20-30 degrees of knee flexion and the entire femur accessible for imaging.

setup.text: Prepare the full limb, ensure the incision can be lengthened enough for atraumatic patellar mobilization, and plan lateral plate insertion and proximal percutaneous fixation before draping.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the patella, patellar tendon, tibial tubercle, lateral joint line, lateral epicondyle, and femoral shaft axis.

incision.text: Use a roughly 15-18 cm anterior incision centered at or slightly lateral to midline, extending sufficiently proximal to permit quadriceps release and medial patellar dislocation.

superficial_interval.text: Expose both borders of the quadriceps tendon while preserving the extensor retinaculum over the anterior patella.

deep_interval.text: Divide the lateral retinaculum and quadriceps longitudinally, leaving an 8-10 mm lateral cuff at the patella; carry the split toward the lateral patellar-tendon border and dislocate the patella medially with knee flexion.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, lateral retinaculum, quadriceps tendon, capsule and synovium, then distal femoral articular surface.

structures_encountered.text: Quadriceps tendon, lateral patellar retinaculum, patella, patellar tendon, synovium, femoral condyles, trochlea, menisci, and cruciate region are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Patellar tendon insertion, articular cartilage, menisci, lateral superior genicular artery, and extensor-mechanism blood supply are at risk.

danger_zones.text: An incision or quadriceps split that is too short concentrates force at the patellar tendon during medial dislocation and can cause avulsion; lengthen the exposure rather than applying force.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the extensor mechanism gradually with the knee flexed; avoid focal pressure on patellar cartilage and excessive tension at the tibial tubercle.

exposure.text: Provides broad visualization of the distal femoral articular surface and lateral condyle while supporting lateral submuscular plate insertion.

limitations.text: Posterior condylar fragments may still need a fragment-specific exposure, and the approach disrupts the extensor mechanism more than a limited lateral plate approach.

extensions.text: Extend proximally through the quadriceps split, add a separate proximal lateral window for plate control, or use small aligned stab incisions for percutaneous screws.

indications.text: Use for intra-articular distal femoral fractures requiring direct reconstruction of the articular block and lateral fixation, including selected lateral sagittal or coronal patterns.

relative_contraindications.text: Prefer a more limited lateral exposure when no articular visualization is needed, and use a fragment-specific medial or posterior approach when the target cannot be seen safely from the lateral parapatellar corridor.

implant_implications.text: The approach accommodates lateral locked plating through a submuscular tunnel; confirm the proximal plate is centered before placing remaining proximal screws.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Obtain unobstructed AP, lateral, and oblique views to verify articular reduction, alignment, plate centering, screw length, and absence of joint penetration.

closure.text: Repair quadriceps tendon and the retained lateral parapatellar cuff with interrupted heavy sutures, restore retinacular continuity, then close subcutaneous tissue and skin.

complications.text: Complications include patellar-tendon avulsion, extensor weakness or adhesions, stiffness, articular malreduction, infection, nonunion, malalignment, and hardware irritation.

bailouts.text: If the patella will not dislocate without excessive tension, extend the skin and quadriceps releases; add a fragment-specific approach if posterior or medial reduction remains unseen.

procedure_applications.condition: A complete or complex intra-articular distal femur fracture requires broad visualization of the articular block with lateral plate access

questions.question: Why must the incision and quadriceps split be long enough?
questions.answer: To permit medial patellar dislocation without avulsing the patellar tendon.

questions.question: How much retinacular cuff is retained beside the patella?
What vessel may be encountered laterally?
questions.answer: The lateral superior genicular artery, which may require avoidance or ligation.
